Posterior of the risk elevation from the total event count

Source: R/canary_post.R
canary_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of a metric of the difference in event risk between study drug and control (rate ratio, risk difference or odds ratio) from the blinded total event count, with the method of Gould and Wang (2017), which uses external information about the control event rate.

Usage

canary_post(
  y,
  n,
  k = 1,
  prior_c,
  metric = c("ratio", "difference", "odds"),
  metric_prior = NULL,
  likelihood = c("binomial", "poisson"),
  crit = NULL,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Total number of subjects with the event (binomial) or of events (Poisson) in the blinded data.

n

Number of subjects (binomial) or total exposure (Poisson).

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to control (k:1).

prior_c

Parameters of the prior of the control event probability (c(a, b) of a Beta distribution, binomial) or rate (shape and rate of a Gamma distribution, Poisson).

metric

One of "ratio", "difference" and "odds"; only "ratio" is available for the Poisson likelihood.

metric_prior

c(meanlog, sdlog) of the lognormal prior of the ratio or odds ratio, or NULL for the default (see Details). Ignored for the difference.

likelihood

"binomial" or "poisson".

crit

Critical value of the metric; by default 1 for the ratio and the odds ratio and 0 for the difference.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible interval of the metric.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles are not computed (they are NA).

control

List of settings of the numerical integration, as in exptime_post (n_u is not used for the Poisson likelihood).

Value

An object of class bssd_post with model "CANARY", prob (posterior probability that the metric exceeds crit), signal, rr (posterior mean, median and credible interval of the metric), estimates (posterior means of the control and study drug probabilities or rates and of the metric), labels and settings, data, prior and integration.

Details

Binomial likelihood. Of \(N\) subjects, \(N_d = \mathrm{round}(k N / (k + 1))\) are on study drug and \(N_c = N - N_d\) on control (the expected arm sizes, as in Gould and Wang, 2017). The total count \(X\) is the sum of independent \(\mathrm{Binomial}(N_d, p_d)\) and \(\mathrm{Binomial}(N_c, p_c)\) counts, and its probability is the convolution of the two. The control probability has the prior \(p_c \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a, b)\). The metric is

  • "ratio": \(R = p_d / p_c\) with a lognormal prior truncated to \(R \le 1 / p_c\), as in the code of Gould and Wang (2017);

  • "odds": the odds ratio \(Q\) with a lognormal prior;

  • "difference": \(D = p_d - p_c\) with a uniform prior on \((-p_c, 1 - p_c)\), which is a uniform prior on \(p_d\) independent of \(p_c\).

The two-dimensional posterior is integrated on \(\mathrm{logit}(p_c)\) (Gauss-Legendre quadrature) and the logarithm of the metric, or \(p_d\) for the difference (Chebyshev interpolation). For each node of \(\mathrm{logit}(p_c)\), the interval of the second coordinate that holds the conditional posterior mass is located separately; for the ratio it ends at the truncation point \(R = 1 / p_c\). The Gauss-Legendre rule is split where the posterior probability of the metric has a kink (\(p_c = 1 / crit\) for the ratio, \(p_c = 1 - crit\) or \(p_c = -crit\) for the difference), so that the results stay accurate when the event probabilities are large.

Poisson likelihood. With the total exposure \(E\) (n) and the control event rate \(\lambda_c\) per unit of exposure, \(X \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(E \lambda_c (1 + k R) / (k + 1))\) with \(\lambda_c \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(a, b)\) (shape and rate) and a lognormal prior on \(R\). The control rate is integrated out analytically and the posterior of \(\log R\) is integrated numerically. Gould and Wang (2017) write the model with the expected number of control events; their Gamma prior with rate \(b'\) on that number corresponds to \(b = b' E / (k + 1)\). The likelihood is that of the BDRIBS model (bdribs_post); only the prior of the rate ratio differs.

The default metric_prior is the lognormal distribution with mean 1 and probability 0.95 between 0.1 and 10 (Gould and Wang, 2017, Section 3.1); elicit_prior(c(0.1, 10), 0.95, "lnorm", mean = 1) gives its parameters. A signal is declared when \(P(M > crit \mid X) > \) cutoff.

References

Gould, A. L. and Wang, W. B. (2017). Monitoring potential adverse event rate differences using data from blinded trials: the canary in the coal mine. Statistics in Medicine, 36(1), 92–104. doi:10.1002/sim.7129

See also

signal_count and count_oc for the critical event counts and their operating characteristics.

Examples

# 12 subjects with the event among 100, control prior Beta(1, 49)
canary_post(y = 12, n = 100, prior_c = c(1, 49))
#> Model: CANARY 
#> Tested quantity: ratio R = p_d / p_c of the event probabilities
#> P(R > 1 | data) = 0.8417
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of R: mean 3.156, median 2.389, 95% interval (0.3521, 10.53)
# the same data with the risk difference
canary_post(y = 12, n = 100, prior_c = c(1, 49), metric = "difference")
#> Model: CANARY 
#> Tested quantity: difference D = p_d - p_c of the event probabilities
#> P(D > 0 | data) = 0.9956
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): yes
#> Posterior of D: mean 0.2108, median 0.2113, 95% interval (0.06536, 0.3504)
